Vladimir Putin announces that Russia and the United States have officially agreed to restore diplomatic relations. A four-hour summit between the US and Russia is held in Saudi Arabia.
links: February 2025 United States–Russia summit in Saudi Arabia

events.text: Egypt announces the discovery of Thutmose II's tomb by a joint British-Egyptian team, the first royal tomb to be discovered since Tutankhamun's in 1922. It is the 15th and final pharaoh tomb from the Eighteenth Dynasty of Egypt to have been found by archeologists.
Croatia completes the process of joining the European Economic Area.

2025 German federal election: After being pushed forward as a result of the 2024 German government crisis, the centre-right CDU/CSU becomes the largest party, with big gains from the far-right AfD, resulting in a second-place finish.
An Antonov An-26 of the Sudanese Air Force crashes in a residential area, near the Wadi Seidna Air Base. All 17 occupants onboard and 29 people on the ground died.
links: 2025 Sudanese Air Force Antonov An-26 crash

events.text: The Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) leader Abdullah Öcalan, made the call for the dissolution of the organization and the laying down of arms from İmralı Prison. The PKK, in turn, declared a ceasefire on 1 March 2025.

A meeting between U.S. president Donald Trump and Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy takes place at the White House. Trump and V.P. JD Vance sharply criticise Zelenskyy, raising questions about support for Ukraine, a proposed end to the war, and the country's future in general.
links: Vice President of the United States

events.text: Firefly Aerospace becomes the first commercial company to successfully land on the Moon with no technical issues, with its Blue Ghost Mission 1.
The Trump administration pauses military aid to Ukraine, following the Oval Office meeting with Zelenskyy the previous week.
links: List of military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian war

events.text: Colossal Biosciences creates woolly mice as part of de-extinction efforts for the woolly mammoth.

Sudan files an application against the United Arab Emirates before the International Court of Justice, alleging violations of the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide by the UAE through its support for the RSF, which is responsible for the genocide in Darfur.
links: Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide

events.text: More than 1,000 people, including civilians, are reported killed in a crackdown by Syrian transitional government security forces in the Alawite region, described as the country's worst violence for years.
The 2025 Special Olympics World Winter Games are held in Turin, Italy.
2025 Greenlandic general election: The center-right Democrats become the largest party, defeating the incumbent Inuit Ataqatigiit.

Balochistan Liberation Army militants blow up railway tracks and hijack the Jaffar Express train bound from Quetta to Peshawar, taking 450 people hostages including both security personnel and civilians.
The former President of the Philippines, Rodrigo Duterte, is arrested in the Philippines after being served an arrest warrant from the International Criminal Court for crimes against humanity.
links: International Criminal Court investigation in the Philippines

events.text: 2025 Belizean general election: The incumbent People's United Party wins a second term in a landslide victory.
Keith Rowley resigns as Prime Minister of Trinidad and Tobago after nine years in office, and is succeeded by Stuart Young.
links: Prime Minister of Trinidad and Tobago

events.text: A fire breaks out in a nightclub in Kočani, North Macedonia, killing at least 59 people and injuring 155 others.
The President of Somalia, Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, survives an attack on his convoy by al-Shabaab, killing at least 10 people.
links: Attempted assassination of Hassan Sheikh Mohamud

events.text: Israel launches widespread aerial bombardments and attacks on the Gaza Strip, killing at least 591 people, including children, ending the ceasefire agreement reached in January.
links: March 2025 Israeli attacks on the Gaza Strip

events.text: Nationwide protests erupt across Turkey following the arrest of the mayor of Istanbul, Ekrem İmamoğlu, on charges of corruption and terrorism.
Kirsty Coventry is elected as the 10th, first female and first African President of the International Olympic Committee in the first round of voting in the 144th IOC Session.
links: President of the International Olympic Committee

events.text: A major power outage causes Heathrow Airport in London to completely shut down, with disruption expected to last for days, affecting thousands of flights around the world.
South Korea experiences one of its worst wildfires in modern history; over 87 000 hectares of land are destroyed in South Gyeongsang Province, killing at least 32 people.
A 7.7-magnitude earthquake occurs in Myanmar, resulting in 5,413 killed and 11,402 injured.
The Caribbean guilder is introduced, replacing the Netherlands Antillean guilder as the currency for Curaçao and Sint Maarten.
Fram2 launches aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, becoming the first crewed spaceflight to enter a polar retrograde orbit.
US President Donald Trump issues sweeping trade tariffs on many countries, including a 10% baseline tariff for all imports.
links: Tariffs in the second Trump administration

events.text: Hungary withdraws from the International Criminal Court after Israeli Prime Minister and accused war criminal Benjamin Netanyahu lands in Budapest for a state visit, in defiance of the International Criminal Court's arrest warrant against him.
links: International Criminal Court arrest warrants for Israeli leaders

events.text: Impeachment of Yoon Suk Yeol: The Constitutional Court of Korea unanimously upholds Yoon's impeachment in an 8–0 vote, officially removing him from office.
Colossal Biosciences showcases three grey wolves that are genetically modified to exhibit the characteristics of the dire wolf.
During a concert performance by Rubby Pérez in Santo Domingo, a nightclub roof collapses, killing at least 231 people, including Pérez, and injures more than 200 others.

2025 Gabonese presidential election: Incumbent transitional President Brice Oligui Nguema wins a full term. The election is the first since the 2023 Gabonese coup d'état, and was preceded by a constitutional referendum in 2024.
Expo 2025 is held in Osaka, Japan.
2025 Ecuadorian general election: Incumbent president Daniel Noboa is re-elected for a full term in the second round.
A motorized wooden boat capsizes after catching fire in the Congo River near the town of Mbandaka in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, killing at least 148 people.

The atmosphere of K2-18b, a candidate water world located 124 light-years away, is found to contain large quantities of dimethyl sulfide and/or dimethyl disulfide – two compounds that, on Earth, are only known to be produced by life.
Pope Francis, head of the Catholic Church since 2013, dies at the age of 88. World leaders pay tribute. Many countries declare national mourning.
links: Death and funeral of Pope Francis

events.text: Pakistan backed attackers affiliated with The Resistance Front open fire on a group of tourists after asking their religion at the Baisaran Valley in Jammu and Kashmir, India, killing 26 and injuring at least 20.
An explosion in the Port of Shahid Rajaee, Bandar Abbas, Iran, kills at least 70 people and injures more than 1,000.
The funeral of Pope Francis is attended by delegations from 164 countries, including 82 leaders, and 250,000 members of the public.
links: Death and funeral of Pope Francis

events.text: At least 11 people are killed and at least 32 others are injured in a vehicle-ramming attack at the annual Lapu Lapu Day festival in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada.
2025 Trinidad and Tobago general election: The UNC wins a majority government, defeating the incumbent PNM.

2025 Canadian federal election: Following Justin Trudeau's resignation as prime minister in March, former governor of the Bank of Canada Mark Carney becomes the Prime Minister of Canada. The Liberal Party wins a fourth consecutive election and forms a minority government.
links: governor of the Bank of Canada

events.text: A widespread power outage affects Spain and Portugal for hours. Andorra is affected for a few seconds while southern France is lightly affected.

The Ukraine–United States Mineral Resources Agreement is signed, providing an economic incentive for the US to continue to invest in Ukraine's defence and reconstruction, in exchange for access to the war-torn country's energy and mineral resources.
2025 Singaporean general election: The incumbent People's Action Party led by Lawrence Wong wins reelection in a landslide, retaining a supermajority government.

2025 Malian protests: Hundreds of demonstrators gather in Bamako, Mali, to protest the government's proposed dissolution of political parties and extension of president Assimi Goïta's mandate by 5 years. The protests mark the first pro-democracy demonstrations in the country since the regime took power in 2021.
2025 Australian federal election: The incumbent Labor Party led by Anthony Albanese wins reelection, increasing their majority.

2025 German federal election: Friedrich Merz is elected Chancellor of Germany in the second round of parliamentary voting, hours after being defeated in the first round, a first in post-WWII German history.

2025 conclave: 133 cardinal electors select Robert Francis Prevost as Pope Francis's successor, on the fourth ballot. He takes the name Leo XIV, and becomes the first pope from North America, the first with Peruvian or U.S. citizenship, and the first from the Order of Saint Augustine.
2025 India–Pakistan conflict: India launches several missiles into Pakistani territory in response to the 2025 Pahalgam attack two weeks prior.
The 2025 IIHF World Championship is held in Stockholm, Sweden, and Herning, Denmark, and is won by the United States.
links: United States men's national ice hockey team

events.text: 2025 Albanian parliamentary election: The incumbent Socialist Party led by Edi Rama wins reelection, retaining a majority government.
The Kurdistan Workers' Party announces its dissolution after previously declaring a ceasefire with Turkey.

2025 Philippine general election: The ruling Alyansa para sa Bagong Pilipinas alliance win a narrow majority of the seats in the Senate, while one of its component parties Lakas–CMD wins the plurality of seats in the House of Representatives.
The Eurovision Song Contest 2025 is held in Basel, Switzerland. Austrian contestant JJ wins with the song "Wasted Love".
2025 Romanian presidential election: Following the annulment of the previous election, Bucharest mayor Nicușor Dan wins in the second round, beating George Simion.
2025 Portuguese legislative election: The incumbent Social Democratic Party led by Luís Montenegro wins an increased plurality, but fails to achieve a majority.
The 2025 Surinamese general election is held.
The 2025 Venezuelan parliamentary election is held.
2025 Nigeria floods: More than 500 people are killed, and hundreds more missing after flooding in Mokwa.

Josep-Lluís Serrano Pentinat is sworn in as the new Episcopal Co-Prince of Andorra and Bishop of Urgell after the Vatican accepts the resignation of Joan Enric Vives i Sicília for age limitation reasons.
2025 Polish presidential election: Karol Nawrocki is narrowly elected President of Poland in the second round of voting, beating Rafał Trzaskowski.
Operation Spiderweb: Ukraine launches a large drone attack on Russian military bases. More than 40 aircraft of the Russian Air Force are attacked.
2025 Mongolian protests: Luvsannamsrain Oyun-Erdene resigns as Prime Minister of Mongolia after losing a no-confidence vote in the State Great Khural.
2025 South Korean presidential election: After being pushed forward as a result of the impeachment of Yoon Suk Yeol, Lee Jae Myung wins the election, beating Kim Moon-soo.
people are killed and more than 30 others injured after a gunman opens fire at a school in Graz, Austria.

Air India Flight 171, a London-bound Boeing 787, crashes into a building after take-off from Ahmedabad, India, killing 229 passengers, 12 crew on board, and 19 people on the ground. One passenger survives the crash. It is the first fatal crash and hull loss involving a Boeing 787 Dreamliner.
links: List of aviation accidents and incidents with a sole survivor

events.text: Twelve-Day War: Israel conducts air strikes against Iran's nuclear facilities, killing military commanders including Hossein Salami; Iran retaliates.
The 2025 FIFA Club World Cup is held in the United States, and is won by Chelsea.
The No Kings protests occur across many cities in the U.S., as well as Canada, Europe, Japan and Mexico, against Donald Trump.
The 51st G7 summit is held in Kananaskis, Canada.
An EF5 tornado strikes southeast of Enderlin, North Dakota, becoming the first EF5 tornado globally since May 20, 2013.

Belarusian opposition leader Sergei Tikhanovsky and 13 other political prisoners are released from prison and deported to Lithuania following a pardon as a result of negotiations with Trump's envoy in Minsk.
Twelve-Day War: The United States carries out B-2 bomber airstrikes on three Iranian nuclear sites in Fordow, Natanz, and Isfahan.
links: 2025 United States strikes on Iranian nuclear sites

events.text: Iran launches missiles at Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar in response to the previous day's U.S. strikes.
links: 2025 Iranian strikes on Al Udeid Air Base

events.text: A NATO summit is held at the World Forum in The Hague, Netherlands.

The Axiom Mission 4 is launched. The mission involves four astronauts, including the first astronauts from Poland (Sławosz Uznański-Wiśniewski) and India (Shubhanshu Shukla) since the end of the Cold War.
The U.S., with Qatari support, brokers a preliminary peace treaty between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda, ending their armed conflict that started in 2022.
links: 2025 Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda peace agreement
Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda conflict (2022–present)

events.text: 2025 Thai political crisis: The Constitutional Court of Thailand suspends Prime Minister Paetongtarn Shinawatra from duty pending a case seeking her dismissal.
At least 135 people are killed and over a hundred reported missing during a flood in Central Texas, United States.
The 2025 World Aquatics Championships are held in Singapore.
Several clashes erupt in southern Syria between armed Druze and Bedouin groups.
Israeli airstrikes hit the Syrian Presidential Palace and the Syrian General Staff headquarters in Damascus.
Twenty-eight countries issue a joint statement calling for an immediate end to the Gaza war, saying it has "reached new depths" in terms of the suffering of civilians.
2025 Dhaka Chengdu J-7 crash: An F-7 BGI training aircraft of the Bangladesh Air Force crashes into Milestone College in Uttara, Dhaka, killing 31 people including the pilot.
The International Court of Justice (ICJ) rules that countries can sue each other over historical emissions of greenhouse gases and the effects of climate change.
Armed conflicts break out between Cambodia and Thailand after the escalation of a border dispute. At least 39 people are killed and more than 100,000 displaced due to the conflicts.
Angara Airlines Flight 2311, operated by an Antonov An-24 aircraft, crashes near Tynda in Eastern Siberia, Russia. All 48 people on board are killed.
An Mw link=y 8.8 earthquake strikes off the coast of Russia's Kamchatka Peninsula, triggering tsunami warnings in Japan and Hawaii.
OpenAI's model GPT-5 is released.
The 2025 World Games are held in Chengdu, China.
Armenia and Azerbaijan sign a peace deal to end 37-year-old hostilities regarding the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict.
2025 Russia–United States Summit: US president Donald Trump meets with Russian president Vladimir Putin in Anchorage, Alaska, to discuss a plan for resolving the Russo-Ukrainian war.
The first World Humanoid Robot Games are held in Beijing, China.
A multi-vehicle collision involving a bus carrying migrants deported from Iran, a motorcycle and a truck kills at least 79 people in Herat Province, Afghanistan.
The 2025 Women's Rugby World Cup is held in, and is won by, England.
links: England women's national rugby union team

events.text: Famine is confirmed in Gaza City for the first time after the UN-backed body responsible for monitoring food security raises its classification to Phase 5, the highest and worst level. The IPC says more than 500,000 people are now facing "starvation, destitution and death".

2025 Thai political crisis: The Constitutional Court of Thailand removes Prime Minister Paetongtarn Shinawatra from office for ethical misconduct over leaked phone calls she had with former Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Sen.
Between 370 and 1,000 people are reported killed in a landslide caused by heavy rain that buries the village of Tarasin in the Marrah Mountains of Central Darfur and leaves one survivor.
An earthquake in eastern Afghanistan kills over 2,200 people and injures 3,500.
At least 16 people are killed and over 21 are injured after the Glória funicular derailment in the centre of Lisbon, Portugal.
Mass anti-government protests erupt in Nepal, resulting in at least 22 deaths and hundreds injured. Prime Minister K. P. Sharma Oli resigns the following day amidst the demonstrations.
2024–2025 French political crisis: The Bayrou government collapses after losing a no-confidence vote.
2025 Norwegian parliamentary election: Incumbent Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre's coalition retains their majority.
Israel attacks the Hamas leadership in Doha, Qatar.
links: Israeli airstrike on Hamas leadership in Qatar

events.text: The 80th session of the United Nations General Assembly opens in New York City, United States.
links: Eightieth session of the United Nations General Assembly

events.text: Russian drone incursion into Poland: Multiple drones breach Polish airspace during a large-scale Russian attack on Ukraine and are intercepted by Polish and NATO forces, marking the first attack on NATO territory and prompting Poland to invoke Article 4.
links: September 2025 Russian drone incursion into Poland
Article 4 of the North Atlantic Treaty

events.text: A liquid petroleum gas truck overturns and explodes at an overpass in Iztapalapa, Mexico City, killing 32 people and injuring 90 others.

Charlie Kirk, an American right-wing activist and influential ally of President Trump, is assassinated at a campus event in Utah, prompting widespread reactions and reprisals both domestically and internationally.
links: Reprisals against commentators on the Charlie Kirk assassination

events.text: The Supreme Federal Court convicts former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro and sentences him to 27 years in prison for his involvement in the 2022 Brazilian coup plot.

Former chief justice Sushila Karki assumes office as interim prime minister of an interim government formed after K. P. Sharma Oli's resignation in Nepal, the decision notably being decided via a poll on a social media platform, Discord.
The 2025 FIVB Men's Volleyball World Championship is held in Pasay and Quezon City, the Philippines, and is won by Italy.
The 2025 World Athletics Championships are held in Tokyo, Japan.
A UN Human Rights Council commission of inquiry finds that Israel has committed genocide against Palestinians in Gaza.
links: 2025 UNHRC Commission of Inquiry report on Gaza genocide

events.text: 2025 Malawian general election: Peter Mutharika is elected president for a second non-consecutive term.
Estonian airspace near Vaindloo island is violated by three Russian MiG-31 jets. In response, Estonia invokes Article 4 of NATO.
links: Article 4 of the North Atlantic Treaty

events.text: Intervision 2025 is held in Moscow, Russia. Vietnamese contestant Đức Phúc wins with the song "".
The UK, Canada, and Australia announce their formal recognition of Palestine as a sovereign state, with France also doing so the next day.

Thousands of protesters across the Philippines gather at the EDSA Shrine in Quezon City for the Trillion Peso March and at Luneta Park in Manila for the Baha sa Luneta demonstrations, demanding government accountability over alleged corruption in flood control and infrastructure projects.
links: Flood control projects scandal in the Philippines

events.text: 2025 Karur crowd crush: At least 40 people are killed and 51 injured in a crowd crush at a rally held by actor-turned-politician Vijay's party Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) in Karur, Tamil Nadu, India.
2025 Moldovan parliamentary election: Incumbent pro-European party PAS wins reelection, forming another majority government.
A Mw link=y 6.9 earthquake shakes the island of Cebu in the Philippines, leaving 71 people dead and 559 injured.
Israel intercepts the Global Sumud Flotilla, a fleet carrying humanitarian aid to the Gaza Strip, in international waters, arresting 443 activists from 47 countries.
Henri, Grand Duke of Luxembourg, abdicates the throne in favor of his son Guillaume.
links: Abdication of Henri, Grand Duke of Luxembourg
Guillaume V, Grand Duke of Luxembourg

events.text: 2025 Czech parliamentary election: ANO leader and former Prime Minister Andrej Babiš wins a plurality of seats, but fails to reach a majority. Incumbent Prime Minister Petr Fiala's coalition fails to win a majority.
Dame Sarah Mullally is named the first female Archbishop of Canterbury.
The 2025 Syrian parliamentary election is held, the first since the fall of the Assad regime in 2024.
Israel and Hamas agree to the first phase of a Gaza peace deal, paving the way for a ceasefire, almost exactly two years after the conflict began.
2025 Afghanistan–Pakistan conflict: Pakistan reportedly carries out airstrikes in Kabul, Khost, Jalalabad, and Paktika, targeting Noor Wali Mehsud, an internationally designated terrorist.
2025 Seychellois general election: Incumbent President Wavel Ramkalawan loses reelection to Patrick Herminie. Ramkalawan's party LDS also loses its majority in parliament.
Dina Boluarte, the President of Peru, is unanimously impeached by the Congress of the Republic.
links: Congress of the Republic of Peru

events.text: 2025 Malagasy coup d'état: Following a series of protests, incumbent President Andry Rajoelina is ousted and military officer Michael Randrianirina becomes President.
2025 Cameroonian presidential election: Incumbent President Paul Biya is re-elected for an eighth consecutive term.

Gaza war: Hamas releases the last 20 living hostages in Gaza after they were kidnapped during the 2023 October 7 attacks. In exchange, Israel releases 250 Palestinian prisoners and more than 1,700 detainees.
Microsoft ends support for Windows 10 that started in 2015.
2025 Louvre heist: Pieces of the French Crown Jewels are stolen during a robbery from the Galerie d'Apollon of the Louvre in Paris.

2025 Bolivian general election: Rodrigo Paz wins the presidential election in a runoff against former President Jorge Quiroga. Incumbent party MAS-IPSP loses all their seats in the Senate and all but two seats in the Chamber of Deputies.
Sanae Takaichi becomes the first female Prime Minister of Japan.
American Eric Lu wins the quinquennial XIX International Chopin Piano Competition at the National Philharmonic in Warsaw, Poland.
2025 Irish presidential election: Independent candidate Catherine Connolly wins the election in a landslide, defeating Fine Gael candidate Heather Humphreys.
2025 Argentine legislative election: Incumbent President Javier Milei's party La Libertad Avanza wins the election with over 40% of the votes.
El Fashir massacre: Mass murder is reported during which an estimated 2,500 or more civilians have been executed by the Rapid Support Forces in the city of El Fashir, Sudan.
Timor-Leste becomes the 11th member state of ASEAN, being the first enlargement of ASEAN since Cambodia's entry in 1999 and comprising all countries of Southeast Asia.
Hurricane Melissa makes a catastrophic landfall in Jamaica as a Category 5 hurricane, with sustained wind speeds up to , becoming the strongest hurricane to strike the country in recorded history.
Operation Containment: In Rio de Janeiro, more than 120 people are killed in raids targeting criminal organization Comando Vermelho during the deadliest police operation in Brazilian history.
2025 Dutch general election: Social liberal party Democrats 66 ties with right-wing populist party Party for Freedom in most number of seats.
A powerful Mw link=y 6.3 earthquake shakes the provinces of Balkh and Samangan in Afghanistan, causing 31 deaths and 956 injuries.
Typhoon Kalmaegi leaves more than 288 people dead in the Philippines, Vietnam, and Thailand.

UPS Airlines Flight 2976, a Honolulu-bound McDonnell Douglas MD-11F, crashes shortly after take-off near Louisville Muhammad Ali International Airport in Kentucky, United States, killing all three crew members and 12 people on the ground, as well as injuring 22 others.
Khaled El-Enany is elected the new Director-General of UNESCO.
The COP30 summit is held in Belém, Brazil, focusing on the role of the Amazon rainforest in climate action.
2025 Delhi Red Fort blast: At least 15 people are killed and more than 20 people are injured in a car explosion near the Red Fort in Delhi.
2025 Iraqi parliamentary election: Incumbent Prime Minister Mohammed Shia' al-Sudani's party RDC wins a plurality of seats.
The New Glenn rocket booster lands for the first time.
Former prime minister of Bangladesh Sheikh Hasina is found guilty of crimes against humanity by a Bangladeshi tribunal and sentenced to death in absentia.
The 2025 FIFA Futsal Women's World Cup is held in the Philippines, and is won by Brazil.
The G20 Johannesburg summit is held in South Africa, the first time a G20 summit has been held in Africa.
2025 Guinea-Bissau general election: A coup d'état occurs a day before the official results release, overthrowing President Umaro Sissoco Embaló.
The second round of the 2025 Egyptian parliamentary election is held.
A report published by the United Nations shows that Indonesian capital Jakarta has surpassed Japanese capital Tokyo as the world's largest city, with a population of 42 million people.
A massive fire engulfs the Wang Fuk Court apartment block in Hong Kong, killing at least people and leaving over 150 missing.
The 2025 World Women's Handball Championship is held in Germany and the Netherlands, and is won by Norway.
Cyclone Senyar causes at least 1,390 deaths and leaves 186 missing in Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia.
An ecumenical meeting of the Eastern Orthodox Church and Catholic Church at Nicaea is held to mark the 1,700th anniversary of the First Council of Nicaea.
links: Visit by Pope Leo XIV to Turkey and Lebanon

events.text: Flooding and landslides caused by Cyclone Ditwah leave at least 647 dead and 183 missing across Sri Lanka and South India.

2025 Honduran general election: Amid allegations of fraud and external interference, National candidate Nasry Asfura narrowly wins the presidency after weeks of delays. The National Party additionally wins a plurality in the National Congress.
The 2025 Kyrgyz parliamentary election is held.
Yemeni civil war: The Southern Transitional Council launches a large-scale military offensive across Southern Yemen, breaking years of military stalemate in the conflict.
A fire at a nightclub in Arpora, Goa, India, leaves at least 25 people dead and 50 injured.
Eleven are killed, including three young children, and fourteen are injured in a shooting at a bar in Saulsville, Gauteng, South Africa.

Elements of the Benin Armed Forces, led by Pascal Tigri, announce a coup d'état against president Patrice Talon and the creation of a military junta after seizing state television. However, the coup attempt is thwarted and unsuccessful.
A Mw link=y 7.6 earthquake occurs in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Aomori Prefecture in Japan, triggering a tsunami up to 70 cm high.
Bulgarian political crisis (2021–2026): The Zhelyazkov Government resigns following major protests.
The Junior Eurovision Song Contest 2025 is held in Tbilisi, Georgia. French contestant Lou Deleuze wins with the song "Ce monde".

Belarus releases 123 political prisoners including opposition leaders Maria Kalesnikava, Maxim Znak, Viktar Babaryka, Nobel laureate Ales Bialiatski, and journalists Pavel Sevyarynets and Marina Zolotova in exchange for the lifting of sanctions on the Belarusian potash industry by the United States.

At least 16 people are killed and 43 injured in a mass shooting, classified as a terrorist attack, by two gunmen at Bondi Beach in Sydney during a celebration for the start of the Jewish festival of Hanukkah.
2025 Chilean general election: José Antonio Kast is elected President of Chile. Right-wing coalitions gain control of the Chamber of Deputies and tie in the Senate.
EU leaders approve a €90bn ($105bn) loan for Ukraine for the next two years, which Kyiv will repay only once Russia pays reparations.
German engineer Michaela Benthaus becomes the first wheelchair user to travel into space, aboard the Blue Origin NS-37.
The 2025 Africa Cup of Nations is held in Morocco, and is won by Senegal.
Harmony Jets Flight 185, a Dassault Falcon 50, crashes near Ankara, Turkey, killing all eight people on board, including Libyan Army chief of staff Mohammed al-Haddad.

The United States, in cooperation with the Nigerian government, initiates a series of airstrikes targeting Islamic State-affiliated militants operating in the country's Sokoto State. US President Donald Trump states that rising extremist violence against Christians is a primary reason for the strikes.
Israel becomes the first country to recognize Somaliland.
2025 Guinean presidential election: Interim president and 2021 coup d'état leader Mamady Doumbouya wins the presidency in a landslide.
2025 Central African general election: Incumbent president Faustin-Archange Touadéra wins reelection for a third term.
December 2025 Kosovan parliamentary election: Incumbent Prime Minister Albin Kurti's party Vetëvendosje wins a fourth consecutive victory, getting 49% of the vote.

2025 Iranian protests: Major protests emerge in Iran following an intense inflation spike that saw a severe depreciation in the Iranian rial. These protests are accompanied with demands for an end to the Islamic republic.
Cyprus begins its role as President of the Council of the European Union.
41 people are killed and 116 injured in a fire at a bar in Crans-Montana, Switzerland.
Bulgaria adopts the euro, becoming the 21st member state of the eurozone.
Equatorial Guinea moves its capital from Malabo to Ciudad de la Paz.
The United States launches several airstrikes on multiple locations across northern Venezuela, capturing Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro and first lady Cilia Flores.
Delcy Rodríguez is formally sworn in as the acting president of Venezuela after the capture of Nicolás Maduro.
Fighting between Syrian government forces and the Kurdish armed group Syrian Democratic Forces begins.
The 2025 Jubilee ends.
The United States seizes two shadow fleet tankers, including one under a Russian flag, in the United States oil blockade during Operation Southern Spear.
links: United States oil blockade during Operation Southern Spear

events.text: Iran retaliates against nationwide protests, with tens of thousands reportedly killed on the 8th and 9th alone, and many thousands more detained amid a severe government crackdown.
Thongloun Sisoulith is re-elected as the General Secretary of the Lao People's Revolutionary Party at the 12th Central Committee's first meeting.
links: General Secretary of the Lao People's Revolutionary Party
12th Central Committee of the Lao People's Revolutionary Party

events.text: 2025–2026 Southern Yemen campaign: The Southern Transitional Council announces its dissolution following territorial losses, including its capital Aden.
The 2026 Beninese parliamentary election is held.

Operation Arctic Endurance is launched by Denmark, with multiple European countries sending troops to Greenland in response to US President Donald Trump's threats of invasion or annexation of the island.

2026 Ugandan general election: Incumbent President Yoweri Museveni wins reelection amidst protests over allegations of election fraud, leading to deaths of dozens of protestors and the abduction of main opposition candidate Bobi Wine.
A fire at a shopping mall in Karachi, Pakistan, kills 80 people.
people are killed and 292 are injured after two trains derail in Adamuz in southern Spain.
The 56th World Economic Forum begins in Davos, Switzerland.

Islamic State insurgency in Afghanistan: Seven people are killed and twenty others injured in a bombing at a Chinese restaurant in Shahr-e Naw, Kabul, Afghanistan. The Islamic State – Khorasan Province claims responsibility.
The Syrian transitional government captures most of the territory held by the Syrian Democratic Forces following an offensive and subsequent ceasefire.
links: Democratic Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria

events.text: The United States officially leaves the World Health Organization.
France seizes one shadow fleet tanker, under a Russian flag, in the Mediterranean.
50 people are killed when a boat capsizes in Malta during Storm Harry. The Italian coastguard estimates a further 380 migrants who set off from Tunisia also drowned during the storm.
links: Corps of the Port Captaincies – Coast Guard

events.text: Tô Lâm is re-elected as the General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam at the 14th National Congress.
links: General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam
14th National Congress of the Communist Party of Vietnam

events.text: The 56th World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland ends.
Iliana Iotova becomes the first female President of Bulgaria after the resignation of Rumen Radev.
At least 70 people are killed and 10 others missing after major landslides in West Java, Indonesia.

2025–26 Myanmar general election: In an election widely considered as neither free nor fair, the pro-military Union Solidarity and Development Party wins a supermajority of seats in the Pyithu Hluttaw and the Amyotha Hluttaw.
The body of Ran Gvili, the last remaining Israeli hostage in the Gaza Strip, is recovered by the IDF from northern Gaza, thus ending the Gaza war hostage crisis.
The India–European Union Free Trade Agreement is signed after nearly two decades of negotiations, eliminating Tariffs on a broad range of products and services between the two regions.
Successive mine collapses at the Rubaya coltan mine in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo kill more than 600 people.
Storm Kristin causes a catastrophic impact in Portugal and Spain with €6 billion in damage in the central region of Portugal, 15 deaths and 2,000 injuries.
Sarah Mullally becomes the first female primate of the Church of England and Archbishop of Canterbury.
Insurgency in Balochistan: Fighting between the Balochistan Liberation Army and the Pakistani armed forces in several districts of Balochistan, Pakistan, leaves at least 225 people dead.
Ethiopian civil conflict: Clashes erupt in the Tigray region in Ethiopia between Tigrayan fighters and Federal Forces.
Three million pages related to the Epstein files are released to the public, mentioning many high-profile public figures worldwide.
links: Prominent individuals mentioned in the Epstein files

events.text: 2026 Costa Rican general election: Laura Fernández Delgado is elected president of Costa Rica, and her party additionally wins a majority in the Legislative Assembly.
Boko Haram insurgency: Boko Haram attacks two villages in Kwara State, Nigeria, killing at least 162 people.
The New START treaty limiting strategic nuclear weapons between the United States and Russia expires.
At least 31 people are killed and another 100 are injured in a suicide bombing at the Khadija Tul Kubra Mosque in Islamabad, Pakistan.
The 2026 Winter Olympics are held in Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo, Italy.
The 2026 Men's T20 World Cup held in India and Sri Lanka begins.
The Transitional Presidential Council of Haiti is dissolved, transferring executive power to acting prime minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé.

2026 Thai general election and constitutional referendum: Incumbent Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul wins a plurality in the House of Representatives, and the Referendum to begin drafting a new constitution passes.
2026 Portuguese presidential election: Socialist candidate António José Seguro is elected President of Portugal in the second round, beating Chega leader André Ventura.
2026 Japanese general election: Incumbent Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi wins a landslide victory, securing a supermajority in the House of Representatives.
At least nine people, including the perpetrator, are killed, and 27 are injured in a mass shooting at Tumbler Ridge Secondary School and at a residence in Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia, Canada.
2026 Barbadian general election: Incumbent Prime Minister Mia Mottley wins every seat in the House of Assembly in a landslide victory.

2026 Bangladeshi general election and constitutional referendum: The Bangladesh Nationalist Party led by Tarique Rahman wins a supermajority in the Jatiya Sangsad, and the referendum on the July Charter passes.
The 62nd Munich Security Conference is held.
The AI Impact Summit takes place in New Delhi, India.
President of Peru José Jerí is censured by the Congress of Peru, removing him from office. He is succeeded by José María Balcázar.
links: Congress of the Republic of Peru

events.text: Kim Jong Un is re-elected as the General Secretary of the Workers' Party of Korea at the 9th National Congress.
links: General Secretary of the Workers' Party of Korea
9th Congress of the Workers' Party of Korea

events.text: 2026 Jalisco operation: A military operation in Tapalpa, Jalisco, Mexico, kills 62 people including Jalisco New Generation Cartel leader El Mencho.
The 2026 Laotian parliamentary election is held.
2025–2026 Dutch cabinet formation: Rob Jetten is sworn in as Prime Minister of the Netherlands, heading a minority government.
2026 Afghanistan–Pakistan war: The government of Pakistan declares "open war" against the Taliban in Afghanistan.
2026 Zona da Mata floods: Floods and landslides in the Zona da Mata region of Minas Gerais, Brazil leave at least 70 people dead and thousands of others displaced.

2026 Iran war: Israel and the United States launch attacks on Iran, killing many high-profile officials, including Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei. Iran launches retaliatory strikes against Israel, as well as against US military bases in the Persian Gulf, and closes the Strait of Hormuz by attacking vessels that try to pass.
links: List of Iranian officials killed during the 2026 Iran war

events.text: Abiemnom massacre: At least 169 people are killed and 50 injured when armed youth from Unity State attack Abiemnom County in South Sudan.
2026 Lebanon war: Hezbollah begins launching strikes against Israel in retaliation for the assassination of Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei.
2026 Iran war: The United States nuclear submarine sinks the Iranian warship IRIS Dena in the Indian Ocean, off Sri Lanka with a torpedo, resulting in 140 sailors missing.
2026 Nepalese general election: The Rastriya Swatantra Party led by Balen Shah wins a landslide victory.
The 2026 World Baseball Classic is held in Japan and the United States.
2026 Kenya floods: At least 66 people are killed after floods across Kenya.
The 2026 Winter Paralympics are held in Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo, Italy.
India beats New Zealand in the 2026 Men's T20 World Cup final and secures its third title.
2026 Colombian parliamentary election: President Gustavo Petro's party Historic Pact wins a plurality of seats in the Chamber of Representatives and the Senate.
2026 Iranian supreme leader election: Mojtaba Khamenei, the son of Ali Khamenei, is selected as the third Supreme Leader of Iran.
First Secretary of the Communist Party of Cuba Miguel Díaz-Canel confirms that Cuba is in talks with the Trump administration to find solutions to the oil blockade in the country.
links: First Secretary of the Communist Party of Cuba

events.text: 2026 Iran war: The United States Air Force conducts a large bombing raid on Kharg Island, a key oil export hub off the Persian Gulf coast of Iran.
2026 North Korean parliamentary election: General Secretary Kim Jong Un's Workers' Party wins a landslide majority in the Supreme People's Assembly.
links: General Secretary of the Workers' Party of Korea

events.text: 2026 Vietnamese legislative election: The Communist Party led by General Secretary Tô Lâm wins almost all the seats in the National Assembly of Vietnam.
2026 Kazakh constitutional referendum: The new Constitution of Kazakhstan is accepted with 90% in favor.
2026 Republic of the Congo presidential election: Incumbent President Denis Sassou Nguesso wins reelection in a landslide victory.
links: 2026 Republic of the Congo presidential election

events.text: 2026 Kabul hospital airstrike: At least 400 people are killed and more than 250 injured in Pakistani airstrikes on a hospital in Kabul, Afghanistan.
2026 Iran war: Ali Larijani, the Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, is assassinated by an Israeli airstrike.
links: Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council

events.text: The 2026 World Athletics Indoor Championships are held at Kujawsko-Pomorska Arena Toruń in Toruń, BiT City, Kuyavian–Pomeranian Voivodeship, Poland.

2026 Italian constitutional referendum: With a higher-than-expected turnout, voters reject a government-backed constitutional reform that would have separated the career paths of judges and prosecutors and split the High Council of the Judiciary into two bodies.
2026 Slovenian parliamentary election: Incumbent Prime Minister Robert Golob wins a plurality of seats in the National Assembly.
A Lockheed C-130 of the Colombian Aerospace Force crashes near Puerto Leguízamo, Colombia, killing 69 people.
links: 2026 Colombian Air Force Lockheed C-130 crash

events.text: OpenAI announces that their flagship Sora app and API are shutting down. The app is shut down on April 26, and its API shut down on September 24.
2026 Danish general election: Incumbent Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen's coalition loses its majority in the Folketing.
2026 Iran war: Iran's Ministry of Foreign Affairs addresses in a letter to the United Nations that ships not tied to either the United States or Israel can pass through the Strait of Hormuz.
NASA launches the Artemis II lunar flyby mission, marking the first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972.
The crew of Artemis II breaks the record for the furthest humans have ever been from Earth, reaching a maximum distance of 252,756 miles (406,771 km) as they travel around the far side of the Moon.
2026 Iran war: Following an ultimatum from Trump regarding the Strait of Hormuz, the United States and Iran agree on a two-week ceasefire.
2026 Vietnamese presidential election: The National Assembly of Vietnam elects General Secretary Tô Lâm as the new president of Vietnam, replacing Lương Cường.
Israel launches a series of airstrikes across Lebanon, targeting Hezbollah infrastructure. More than 300 people are killed and over 1,100 injured.
2026 Djiboutian presidential election: Incumbent President Ismaïl Omar Guelleh is re-elected for a sixth term.

The crew of Artemis II successfully returns to Earth, splashing down safely in the Pacific Ocean near San Diego, California, United States. The four crew members are extracted from the capsule and taken by helicopter to the USS John P. Murtha.
2026 Iraqi presidential election: The Iraqi Parliament elects Nizar Amidi of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) as the new President of Iraq, winning with 227 votes in the second round.
2026 Hungarian parliamentary election: Incumbent Prime Minister Viktor Orbán loses re-election in a landslide to Péter Magyar's Tisza Party, ending 16 years of Fidesz–KDNP rule.
2026 Beninese presidential election: Independent candidate Romuald Wadagni wins in a landslide with over 94% of the vote.

2026 Iran war: A blockade of Iranian ports by the United States takes effect, with President Trump warning that any Iranian vessels attempting to challenge it will be "immediately eliminated". Maritime authorities advise ships in the region to expect increased military activity and possible interception procedures.
links: 2026 United States naval blockade of Iran

events.text: 2026 Lebanon war: A US-brokered 10-day ceasefire takes effect between Israel and Lebanon, following ambassador-level talks in the White House.
2026 Bulgarian parliamentary election: The Progressive Bulgaria coalition, led by former President Rumen Radev, wins a landslide victory, securing 44% of the vote and an outright majority of seats.
2026 Iran war: US President Trump announces a further extension of the ceasefire until an Iranian proposal is submitted and conversations are concluded at the request of Pakistan.
Tornado outbreak sequence of April 23–28, 2026: An EF4 tornado hits the Vance Air Force Base in Enid, Oklahoma, injuring one person and damaging or destroying homes.
2026 Mali offensives: The Azawad Liberation Front and JNIM launch several large-scale attacks, targeting major cities across Mali, capturing Kidal and parts of Gao, Mopti, and Sevare.
The United Arab Emirates leaves OPEC, ending six decades of membership and removing one of the organization's largest oil producers.
An explosion at a fireworks factory in Liuyang, Hunan, China kills 37 people and injures 51 others.

Sudanese civil war: Rapid Support Forces launch drone attacks at several targets in Khartoum, Sudan, including the Khartoum International Airport in Khartoum, Sudan. Drone strikes are also reported at the Signal Corps in Khartoum Bahri and Al-Markhiyat camp in northern Omdurman. Additionally, the Sudan Army's air defenses intercept drone strikes at the airport.
2026 Bahamian general election: Incumbent Prime Minister Philip Davis wins a second term in office.

The Eurovision Song Contest 2026 is held in Vienna, Austria, following their win at the Eurovision Song Contest 2025. Bulgarian contestant Dara wins with the song "Bangaranga", marking the first time Bulgaria has won the contest.
links: Austria in the Eurovision Song Contest
Bulgaria in the Eurovision Song Contest

events.text: Gaza war: An Israeli strike assassinates Izz al-Din al-Haddad, commander of the Izz al-Din al-Qassam Brigades and leader of Hamas in the Gaza Strip.

2026 Ituri Province Ebola epidemic: The World Health Organization declares an Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda a Public Health Emergency of International Concern.
links: Public Health Emergency of International Concern

events.text: 2026 Cape Verdean parliamentary election: Incumbent Prime Minister Ulisses Correia e Silva loses reelection to PAICV leader Francisco Carvalho.
links: African Party for the Independence of Cape Verde

events.text: Former First Secretary of the Communist Party of Cuba Raúl Castro is indicted by the United States over the 1996 shootdown of Brothers to the Rescue aircraft.
links: First Secretary of the Communist Party of Cuba
1996 shootdown of Brothers to the Rescue aircraft

events.text: The 2026 European heatwaves begin, bringing record-breaking temperatures to several European countries and causing thousands of deaths over the next several weeks.
A gas explosion at the Liushenyu coal mine in Shanxi, China, kills 82 people.
2026 Cypriot legislative election: The Democratic Rally led by Annita Demetriou wins a plurality of seats.
2026 Maltese general election: The Labour Party led by incumbent Prime Minister Robert Abela wins their fourth consecutive election.

Flamingo Revolution: Following small protests in the village of Zvërnec, major protests erupt in Albania over a proposed luxury development involving Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner and his firm Affinity Partners, as well as broader discontent with Prime Minister Edi Rama's government.
2026 Guinean parliamentary election: Parties supporting incumbent President Mamady Doumbouya win the election.
2026 Ethiopian general election: The Prosperity Party, led by incumbent Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, wins reelection.

2026 Delhi Jantar Mantar protests: A series of demonstrations takes place in Jantar Mantar, New Delhi, initiated by the Cockroach Janta Party, an Indian youth-based satirical political movement, along with other student organisations.
2026 Armenian parliamentary election: The Civil Contract, led by incumbent Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan, wins reelection.

2026 Peruvian general election: Popular Force leader Keiko Fujimori narrowly defeats Together for Peru leader Roberto Sánchez in the presidential runoff. Left-wing parties gain a majority in the Chamber of Deputies but tie in the reestablished Senate.
2026 Kosovan parliamentary election: Amid the ongoing political deadlock, Vetëvendosje, led by incumbent Prime Minister Albin Kurti, wins a plurality of seats.
A powerful magnitude 7.8 earthquake strikes the Philippines, the strongest in the country since 1976. 107 are killed and 1,319 are injured.
Turkey and Saudi Arabia sign an agreement to revive the 19th century Hejaz railway.

In Barcelona, Spain, the blessing ceremony of the Sagrada Família's tallest tower by Pope Leo XIV is held, exactly 100 years after the death of architect Antoni Gaudí. Pope Leo XIV consecrates and opens the central tower of Jesus Christ. The Sagrada Família is the world's tallest church.

The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration declares the onset of an El Niño event in the tropical Pacific, and forecasts a 63% chance that it will rank among the largest since records began in 1950.
The 2026 FIFA World Cup is held in Canada, Mexico, and the United States, and is won by Spain.
The 2026 Women's T20 World Cup is held in England and Wales, and is won by Australia.
Elon Musk becomes the first US dollar trillionaire with the initial public offering of SpaceX.
The 2026 24 Hours of Le Mans is held in Le Mans, France.

A mid-air collision between two helicopters in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, kills six people, including American singer-songwriter Oliver Tree, Argentine YouTuber Gaspi, Argentine director and screenwriter Lucas A. Vignale and Brazilian music producer Lucas Frota.

The United States and Iran announce and sign the Islamabad Memorandum, a 14-point agreement to end the 2026 Iran war, reopen the Strait of Hormuz, lift the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports, and begin a 60-day negotiation period on Iran's nuclear programme; Israel says it will not withdraw from territory it has seized in southern Lebanon.
2026 Colombian presidential election: Right-wing outsider Abelardo de la Espriella wins the election in a runoff against left-wing candidate Iván Cepeda.
Keir Starmer announces his resignation as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, prompting a leadership election.
links: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom

events.text: Two consecutive earthquakes with magnitudes of Mw link=y, and Mw 7.5 shake western Venezuela. At least 6,300 people are killed, with thousands injured or missing and widespread damage across the country.

2026 Écône consecrations: Members of the Society of Saint Pius X (SSPX) in Écône, Switzerland, consecrate four bishops against the direct orders of Pope Leo XIV, triggering a religious schism between SSPX and the Catholic Church.
The 2026 Algerian parliamentary election is held.
The state funeral of Ali Khamenei, the Supreme Leader of Iran assassinated during the 2026 Iran war, is held.
The inaugural Nations Championship – Southern Hemisphere Series, an international rugby union tournament, is held.
Hamas announces the resignation of its civil administration under the Gaza peace plan.
The 2026 NATO summit is held in Ankara, Turkey.
The International Olympic Committee lifts the ban on the Russian Olympic Committee, allowing its athletes to participate in future Olympic Games.
2026 Iran war: The Islamabad Memorandum between the United States and Iran breaks down, with U.S. President Trump saying the agreement is "over" following renewed U.S. strikes on Iranian targets.
A fire at the Rong Beer Na Lat Phrao live-music venue in Chatuchak district, Bangkok, kills 34 people and injures more than 70 others.
The world record for the mile run is broken by British runner Josh Kerr at the London Athletics Meet, with a time of 3:42.66 surpassing the previous record held by Hicham El Guerrouj since 1999.
2026 São Toméan presidential election: Incumbent President Carlos Vila Nova is reelected for a second term.

2026 FIFA World Cup final: Spain beat defending champions Argentina 1–0 during extra time to win a second FIFA World Cup title after 16 years. Spanish forward Ferran Torres scores the only goal in the 106th minute.
2026 Iran war: The Houthis announce a maritime blockade against Saudi Arabia on the Bab el-Mandeb strait.
Andy Burnham is appointed by King Charles III as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, succeeding Keir Starmer.
links: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom

events.text: Nicaraguan co-president Daniel Ortega announces an end to elections within Nicaragua.

European heatwaves: Wildfires in France, Portugal and Spain force 300,000 people to evacuate their homes. French officials call it the worst wildfire emergency in decades, while officials in Madrid describe it as the worst the region has ever experienced.
The 2026 Commonwealth Games are held in Glasgow, Scotland.
An earthquake strikes Kumamoto Prefecture in southern Japan with a magnitude of Mww 6.8(MJMA 7.1) at a depth of , killing at least 30 and injuring over 60.
The Republic of Nauru officially changes its name to the Republic of Naoero.
An avalanche on Broad Peak in the Karakoram range of Pakistan kills ten climbers, including Nirmal Purja, Pur Bahadur Gurung, Nadhira Al Harthy and Kili Pemba Sherpa.

2026 Ceuta migrant crisis: Approximately 80,000 people illegally enter Ceuta, Spain with smaller numbers attempting to cross into Melilla, having swam from Morocco. This follows a Supreme Court of Spain decision prohibiting the hot return of migrants arriving by sea. At least 111 people are killed.

2026 Iran war: Saudi Arabia announces the establishment of a 14-nation military alliance to restore and protect freedom of navigation through the Red Sea amid the Iran conflict and ongoing crisis in the area stimulated by the Houthis.
Poland wins the 2026 FIVB Men's Volleyball Nations League, held in Ningbo, China, defeating the United States 3–2 in the final.
links: United States men's national volleyball team

events.text: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey sign the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, a mutual defence pact, amid the 2026 Iran war.
A powerful magnitude 7.4 earthquake strikes Colombia, killing 331 and injuring over 1,248 people.
A ferry capsizing on Lake Kariba, Zimbabwe, kills at least 97 people, becoming the deadliest boat disaster in the country's history.

Prosecution of Syrian civil war criminals: A court in Damascus sentences nine Syrian former officials, including ousted president Bashar al-Assad; his brother Maher; his defense minister Fahd Jassem al-Freij; and Atef Najib, former head of the Political Security Directorate in Daraa and Assad's first cousin, to death for premeditated murder, torture and crimes against humanity committed during the Syrian civil war. Except for Najib, all the others were tried in absentia.
links: Prosecution of Syrian civil war criminals

events.text: A total solar eclipse occurs in parts of Europe, the first in continental Europe since 1999.
2026 Zambian general election: Incumbent President Hakainde Hichilema wins reelection, and the UPND wins a majority in the National Assembly.
At least 136 people are killed and nearly 1,300 injured when a magnitude 7.7 earthquake strikes off the island of Flores, Indonesia.
2026 Zamboye mine collapse: More than 100 people are killed in a landslide at an artisanal gold mining site in Zamboye, Nana-Mambéré, Central African Republic, near the border with Cameroon.
2026 Iran war: U.S. President Donald Trump announces an "Economic D-Day" against Iran, calling on allies to join efforts to isolate Iran economically.

Rojava Revolution: The Syrian Democratic Forces announces its integration into the Syrian Army, resulting in the dissolution of the Democratic Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria in favor of the Syrian government under Ahmed al-Sharaa.
links: Democratic Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria

events.text: 2026 Kazakh legislative election: Pro-Tokayev party Ädilet wins a supermajority in the newly established Kurultai.

Aftermath of the Syrian civil war: The US removes Syria and Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham from its list of designated state sponsors of terrorism, lifting restrictions on foreign investments in the country and allowing services like VISA to work in Syria. Syria has been on the list since 1979.
links: Aftermath of the Syrian civil war

events.text: At least 12 are killed and 56 injured, when over 150 wildfires break out in Algeria, prompting calls from the president to reintroduce capital punishment for convicted arsonists, which has not been practiced in the country since 1993.

2026 Nepal–Tibet floods: At least 1,403 people are killed and 6,650 are reported missing after a landslide and glacial collapse trigger flash floods and debris flows at the border between Nepal and the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.
King Harald V of Norway dies and is succeeded by his son, King Haakon VIII.
links: Death and state funeral of Harald V

events.text: 2026 Nigerien coup attempt: A mutinous faction of the Niger Armed Forces called the Armed Forces for the Restoration of the Fatherland attempt a coup against president Abdourahamane Tiani.
2026 Icelandic European Union membership negotiations referendum: A referendum to continue negotiations for Iceland to join the European Union is rejected.
links: 2026 Icelandic European Union membership negotiations referendum

events.text: NASA launches the flagship Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket. Designed to study dark energy, dark matter and exoplanets, the observatory has a field of view at least 100 times larger than the Hubble Space Telescope's.
The 2026 Estonian presidential election: Ülle Madise is elected president of Estonia by the Riigikogu.
2026 Yemen offensives: The Houthis launch a large ground offensive against the internationally recognized Yemeni government forces, ending the ceasefire and resuming the civil war.

The United Nations votes to adopt a resolution which calls for wider use of the Equal Earth projection over the Mercator projection to better reflect the true size of equatorial regions such as Africa.
The 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup is held in Berlin, Germany, and is won by the United States.
links: United States women's national basketball team

events.text: The 2026 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup is held in Łódź, Katowice, Sosnowiec and Bielsko-Biała, Poland, and is won by Spain.
links: Spain women's national under-20 football team

events.text: The Eighty-First session of the United Nations General Assembly opens in New York.
links: Eighty-First session of the United Nations General Assembly

events.text: Twelve countries, including Canada, France and the United Kingdom, announce plans to introduce or support trade restrictions on goods from Israeli settlements, citing threats to a two-state solution.
A fire on the ferry MV June Aster kills at least 76 people and 13 others go missing off Coron, Palawan, Philippines.
2026 Iran war: Saudi Arabia temporarily shuts down the East-West Pipeline following damage sustained from drone strikes launched from Iraqi territory.
2026 Yemen offensives: The Houthis make significant advancements along Yemen's Red Sea coast, taking control of the city of Mokha and the strategic Bab al-Mandeb strait, leading to a shipping crisis.
Indonesian ferry KM Virgo Transport 8 sinks in the Java Sea, killing 64 and leaving 71 missing.
2026 Swedish general election: The left-wing bloc led by former Prime Minister and Social Democratic leader Magdalena Andersson narrowly wins a majority in the Riksdag.

The United States publicly acknowledges for the first time that it has deployed "space control weapons" in Earth orbit, with Air Force Secretary Troy Meink confirming that the United States Space Force possesses orbital weapons capable of offensive and defensive operations.
links: United States Secretary of the Air Force

events.text: Former president and prime minister of Kosovo Hashim Thaçi is sentenced to 25 years in prison for war crimes during his command of the Kosovo Liberation Army, including the murder of 96 people and the torture of 303 people in the Kosovo War.
links: War crimes in the Kosovo War#KLA war crimes

events.text: Leopardus tilcayo, a wild cat native to Bolivia, is reported as the first new feline species formally identified since 1923.

2026 French lycée protests: A series of student led protests begin in the outskirts of Paris with students demanding better funding and resources for schools. In early October these protests had spread across France and into neighboring Belgium, with hundreds of thousands taking part and thousands arrested.

Following months of threats by U.S. President Donald Trump to acquire or annex Greenland, an agreement is announced by Denmark, Greenland and the United States to strengthen security in the Arctic and North Atlantic, expanding the permanent U.S. military presence in Greenland while recognizing Danish sovereignty and Greenlandic self-determination. The agreement is formally signed on September 22.

2026 Russian legislative election: The ruling United Russia led by Dmitry Medvedev and supported by president Vladimir Putin maintains parliamentary majority in an election which saw no significant competition. Western media outlets criticise the election as being rigged or interfered with.
The 2026 Asian Games are held around Aichi Prefecture in Japan.

2026 Ethiopian offensive: The Tigray People’s Liberation Front and groups aligned with them launch a military offensive in northern Ethiopia against the Ethiopian Government, resuming the civil conflict.

2026 Moroccan general election: The Authenticity and Modernity Party led by Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri wins the most seats in the House of Representatives. Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri becomes Morocco's first female prime minister.
2026 Bangkok floods: At least 40 are killed during flooding in Bangkok, Thailand.
Flash flooding and landslides kill at least 56 people in India and at least 14 people in Nepal. For Nepal this occurs one month on from devastating floods.

events.text: G7 leaders hold an emergency meeting to discuss global diesel supplies and agree to release 100 million barrels of oil, as prices surge to record highs amid disruption from the 2026 Iran war.
2026 Latvian parliamentary election: Incumbent Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs's United List wins a plurality of seats in the Saeima.
The 2026 Bosnian general election is held.
Houthi-Saudi conflict: Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia agree to activate the Mecca defense pact in response to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.
2026 Kosovan presidential election: The Assembly of Kosovo elects Justina Shiroka Pula as the new President of Kosovo, ending the 2025–2026 political deadlock.
Houthi-Saudi conflict: At least 20 people are killed and more than 350 others are injured in a series of attacks on airports perpetrated by the Houthis in Riyadh, Abha and Dammam, Saudi Arabia.

events.text: 2026 Djibouti migrant boat sinking: At least 139 people die and 84 remain missing when a migrant boat travelling to Yemen sinks off of Djibouti.

2026 French supermarket refrigerator hack: A major cyberattack targets the refrigeration units of hundreds of supermarkets across France, raising the temperature to 50 °C. The hack results in fires and tens of millions of euros worth of losses from food spoilage. Other countries in Europe are also impacted to a lesser extent. It is the first cyberattack to cause major disruption to a nation's food supply chain.
G20 finance ministers meet with the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank in Thailand to discuss the economic fallout of the Iran War.

events.text: An early bronze age shipwreck off the coast of Turkey which dates between 2400–2700 BC is reported as the world's oldest shipwreck.

At the General Conference on Weights and Measures, the International Bureau of Weights and Measures votes to abolish future leap seconds and make Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) continuous, starting 20 May 2027. To account for future differences between UTC and International Atomic Time, a leap hour will be observed as needed.
